evidence: Invite students to turn and talk to an elbow partner to discuss what they have noticed when they look at the sky and the patterns that they have noticed in these observations: 'What have you noticed when you look at the sky?'
rationale: The standard lists four collaborative acts joined by commas: discuss topics, investigate questions, solve problems, and explore and create texts. These read as an OR-list of ways students "work with others," so satisfying any one suffices for the clause it belongs to — but the standard's backbone is the single skill "work with others" applied across these purposes. Three of four purposes are met. Students discuss topics with partners: "Invite students to turn and talk to an elbow partner to discuss what they have noticed when they look at the sky." Students investigate the guiding question collaboratively through partner discussions and the close read-aloud. Students explore and create a text during the shared writing activity where they contribute ideas: "now they will use their ideas of what the sun and moon look like in a class shared writing activity." However, no activity has students work together to solve a problem, so that purpose is unmet. Because the four purposes function as an OR-list under one skill, meeting any one is sufficient — alignment is full.
standard_raw_text: Work with others to discuss topics, investigate questions, solve problems, and explore and create texts. (I/C)
